- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.

in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",

Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". 1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Fixture ROI-content contract: a fixture whose phase-2 comment promises a
3	# kernel must actually carry that kernel BETWEEN the markers. The compiler
4	# may legally hoist an inlined kernel above enter_vsim() -- the markers'
5	# "memory" clobber does not cover statics whose address never escapes --
6	# which silently empties the ROI (rt_c_matmul shipped that way: markers
7	# back-to-back, window_cycles ~74 of pure drain overhead). Anchor rule
8	# (runtime/rt_c_helpers.h): kernels live in a noinline function called
9	# between the markers.
10	#
11	# Checks (static, objdump):
12	#   rt_c_matmul    span contains the GEMM: a kernel call (jal) or a mul
13	#   rt_c_v_matmul  span contains the kernel call (control: known-good)
14	#   rt_c_v_regs    span contains vector instructions (inline V kernel)
15	set -uo pipefail
16	
17	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
18	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
19	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"
20	
21	OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
22	OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
23	command -v "$OBJDUMP" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "skip[fixture_roi_content]: no objdump"; exit 77; }
24	
25	FIXDIR="$SCRIPT_DIR"
26	
27	# Instructions strictly between the ENTER and EXIT markers.
28	roi_body() {
29	  "$OBJDUMP" -d "$FIXDIR/$1.elf" \
30	    | awk '/5a002013/ { on = 1; next } /5a102013/ { exit } on'
31	}
32	
33	check_roi() {  # $1 = fixture, $2 = required-content regex, $3 = description
34	  BODY=$(roi_body "$1")
35	  if [ -z "$BODY" ]; then
36	    fail "$1: ROI is EMPTY (markers back-to-back) -- kernel hoisted out?"
37	  fi
38	  if ! printf '%s\n' "$BODY" | grep -Eq "$2"; then
39	    echo "--- ROI body of $1 ---"
40	    printf '%s\n' "$BODY"
41	    fail "$1: ROI does not contain $3 (want /$2/)"
42	  fi
43	  ok "$1: ROI carries $3"
44	}
45	
46	check_roi rt_c_matmul   '\sjal\s|\smulw?\s' "the GEMM (kernel call or mul)"
47	check_roi rt_c_v_matmul '\sjal\s'           "the kernel call"
48	check_roi rt_c_v_regs   '\sv[a-z0-9.]+\.v'  "vector instructions"
49	
50	ok "fixture ROI content"
51

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# test_all.sh -- run the full andesim test surface. This is the entry point that
3	# replaced the former `andesim test` subcommand (which moved out of the binary).
4	#
5	# Phases (all run, in order, unless named explicitly):
6	#   unit      build/driver/andesim-*-test   the C++ driver unit tests
7	#   contract  tests/andes_sim/*.sh          driver feature + parity contracts
8	#   e2e       scripts/run_e2e.sh            hybrid qemu+vsim round-trips
9	#
10	# Usage:
11	#   scripts/test_all.sh [--dry-run] [unit|contract|e2e ...]
12	#
13	# --dry-run prints the plan without executing (and without building). The
14	# contract and e2e phases need built artifacts -- run scripts/build_all.sh
15	# first. FILTER / MODE / JOBS pass through to scripts/run_e2e.sh unchanged.
16	set -uo pipefail
17	
18	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
19	
20	DRY_RUN=0
21	PHASES=()
22	for arg in "$@"; do
23	  case "$arg" in
24	    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
25	    unit|contract|e2e) PHASES+=("$arg") ;;
26	    *)
27	      echo "test_all.sh: unknown argument: $arg" >&2
28	      echo "usage: test_all.sh [--dry-run] [unit|contract|e2e ...]" >&2
29	      exit 2
30	      ;;
31	  esac
32	done
33	[ "${#PHASES[@]}" -eq 0 ] && PHASES=(unit contract e2e)
34	
35	step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
36	ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
37	fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
38	
39	pass=0
40	failed=0
41	declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()
42	
43	# run_case NAME CMD...  -- execute one case, tally it, dump its log on failure.
44	run_case() {
45	  local name="$1"; shift
46	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then printf '  %s\n' "$name"; return; fi
47	  local log rc; log=$(mktemp)
48	  "$@" >"$log" 2>&1; rc=$?
49	  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
50	    ok "$name"; pass=$((pass + 1))
51	  else
52	    fail "$name (rc=$rc)"; failed=$((failed + 1)); FAILED_NAMES+=("$name")
53	    cat "$log"
54	  fi
55	  rm -f "$log"
56	}
57	
58	run_unit() {
59	  step "[unit] C++ driver unit tests"
60	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
61	    printf '  %s\n' "scripts/build_driver.sh" "build/driver/andesim-*-test (each)"
62	    return
63	  fi
64	  if ! bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null; then
65	    fail "[unit] build_driver.sh failed"; failed=$((failed + 1)); return
66	  fi
67	  shopt -s nullglob
68	  local bins=("$ROOT"/build/driver/andesim-*-test)
69	  shopt -u nullglob
70	  if [ "${#bins[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
71	    fail "[unit] no unit-test binaries under build/driver"; failed=$((failed + 1)); return
72	  fi
73	  local t
74	  for t in "${bins[@]}"; do run_case "[unit] $(basename "$t")" "$t"; done
75	}
76	
77	run_contract() {
78	  step "[contract] driver feature + parity contracts"
79	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
80	    printf '  %s\n' "tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh (each)" \
81	      "tests/andes_csr/test_*.sh (each)"
82	    return
83	  fi
84	  local s
85	  for s in "$ROOT"/tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh \
86	           "$ROOT"/tests/andes_csr/test_*.sh; do
87	    [ -f "$s" ] || continue
88	    run_case "[contract] $(basename "$s")" bash "$s"
89	  done
90	}
91	
92	run_e2e() {
93	  step "[e2e] hybrid qemu+vsim round-trips"
94	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then printf '  %s\n' "scripts/run_e2e.sh"; return; fi
95	  run_case "[e2e] run_e2e.sh" bash "$ROOT/scripts/run_e2e.sh"
96	}
97	
98	for p in "${PHASES[@]}"; do
99	  case "$p" in
100	    unit)     run_unit ;;
101	    contract) run_contract ;;
102	    e2e)      run_e2e ;;
103	  esac
104	done
105	
106	if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
107	  echo
108	  echo "(dry-run: nothing executed)"
109	  exit 0
110	fi
111	
112	echo
113	step "summary: $pass passed, $failed failed"
114	if [ "$failed" -gt 0 ]; then
115	  fail "failed: ${FAILED_NAMES[*]}"
116	  exit 1
117	fi
118

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Test: make tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.c serve BOTH the marked and the
3	# markerless build from one source.
4	#
5	# Pins three source properties the rest of the GEMM-unification depends on:
6	#   1. noinline kernel  - `vmatmul_kernel` survives -O1 as a real symbol, so
7	#      PC-range assertions can anchor on it.
8	#   2. marker macro     - compiling with -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS drops the
9	#      ROI enter/exit marker HINTs.
10	#   3. behavior-identity - the default (marked) build still emits both markers.
11	#
12	# Self-contained: resolves the Andes toolchain via tests/lib/paths.sh (config.env)
13	# and builds through the fixtures Makefile. Skips (77) if the toolchain is absent.
14	
15	set -uo pipefail
16	
17	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
18	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"
19	
20	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
21	
22	if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ] || [ ! -x "$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc" ]; then
23	  echo "SKIP test_gemm_source: HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set/usable"
24	  exit 77
25	fi
26	CC="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"
27	NM="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm"
28	OBJDUMP="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump"
29	
30	cd "$SCRIPT_DIR"
31	SRC=rt_c_v_matmul.c
32	ELF=rt_c_v_matmul.elf
33	[ -f "$SRC" ] || fail "missing source $SRC"
34	
35	# --- 1. marked build: noinline kernel symbol present -----------------------
36	# NB: feed grep via here-strings, not `cmd | grep -q`. Under `set -o pipefail`
37	# grep -q exits on first match and SIGPIPEs the producer (141), which pipefail
38	# then propagates as a spurious failure on large inputs (e.g. the objdump).
39	make -s TOOLCHAIN="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN" "$ELF" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "make $ELF failed"
40	syms=$("$NM" "$ELF")
41	grep -qw vmatmul_kernel <<<"$syms" \
42	  || fail "noinline broken: 'vmatmul_kernel' is not a symbol in $ELF (still inlined)"
43	ok "marked build keeps vmatmul_kernel as a linkable symbol (noinline)"
44	
45	# --- 2. behavior-identity: marked build still emits both ROI markers --------
46	# Match the instruction OPCODE (toolchain-independent): 5a002013 =
47	# slti x0, x0, 0x5A0 (enter); 5a102013 = slti x0, x0, 0x5A1 (exit) --
48	# the exact encodings insn_match.h drains on.
49	dump=$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$ELF")
50	grep -qw 5a002013 <<<"$dump" \

1	# Shared path resolution for the top-level e2e harness + drivers.
2	# Sourced (not executed). Provides:
3	#   TOP_ROOT                  - absolute path of the repo root
4	#   hybrid_resolve_paths()    - sets VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN,
5	#                               VSIM_ELF from TOP_ROOT (unless already
6	#                               exported by caller) and exits 77 (CTest
7	#                               skip) if any artifact is missing. Reads
8	#                               FIXTURE for the VSIM_ELF default.
9	#   hybrid_describe_int F [BIN] - print integer field F from an engine's
10	#                               --describe JSON (BIN defaults to $VSIM_BIN);
11	#                               empty output if absent/unprobeable. The ONE
12	#                               shell parser of the descriptor wire format.
13	
14	TESTS_LIB_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
15	TOP_ROOT=$(cd -- "$TESTS_LIB_DIR/../.." && pwd)
16	
17	if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ] && [ -f "$TOP_ROOT/config.env" ]; then
18	  . "$TOP_ROOT/config.env"
19	fi
20	
21	hybrid_resolve_paths() {
22	  # VSIM_BIN_DIR / QEMU_BIN_DIR come from the environment or from the
23	  # config.env sourced above; there is no in-tree fallback (both simulators
24	  # are external prebuilts). Unset -> a nonexistent path -> skip below.
25	  VSIM_BIN="${VSIM_BIN:-${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}/sim_ax45mpv_premium}"
26	  VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}/qemu-system-riscv64}"
27	  VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$TOP_ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
28	  VSIM_ELF="${VSIM_ELF:-$TOP_ROOT/tests/fixtures/${FIXTURE}.elf}"
29	  for f in "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_QEMU" "$VSIM_PLUGIN" "$VSIM_ELF"; do
30	    if [ ! -e "$f" ]; then
31	      echo "skip: $f not built; run 'source ./setup.sh' and 'make -C tests/fixtures'"
32	      exit 77
33	    fi
34	  done
35	}
36	
37	# Extract one integer field from an engine's --describe JSON. $1 = field name,
38	# $2 = engine binary (default $VSIM_BIN). Prints nothing when the field is
39	# absent or the binary cannot be probed, so callers can `[ -n ... ]`-gate.
40	hybrid_describe_int() {
41	  "${2:-$VSIM_BIN}" --describe 2>/dev/null \
42	    | sed -n "s/.*\"$1\": *\([0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1/p" | head -n1
43	}
44	
45	# Write a 32-bit little-endian word into a binary file (pattern staging for
46	# the LM/HVM backdoor-load tests). $1 = file, $2 = byte offset, $3 = value.
47	put_word_le() {
48	  local v=$3 bytes="" i
49	  for i in 0 8 16 24; do
50	    bytes+=$(printf '\\x%02x' $(( (v >> i) & 0xff )))
51	  done
52	  # shellcheck disable=SC2059
53	  printf "$bytes" | dd of="$1" bs=1 seek="$2" conv=notrunc status=none
54	}
